ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the signal-flow graph is from U(s) to Y(s) from left to right. Along the main horizontal line, there are in sequence a gain 1 from the input to the first internal node, s^{-1} from the first internal node to the second internal node, s^{-1} from the second internal node to the third internal node, and a gain 1 from the third internal node to the output. Between the second internal node and the third internal node, there is also an upper parallel forward branch, with gain 1. From the third internal node to the second internal node there is a feedback branch, with gain -4; from the third internal node to the first internal node there is a larger feedback branch, with gain -2. Reasoning: As required, label the three internal nodes from left to right as x1, x2, x3. There are two forward paths from U(s) to Y(s): P1 passes through the s^{-1} branch from x2 to x3, with gain 1·s^{-1}·s^{-1}·1=s^{-2}; P2 passes through the upper gain 1 branch from x2 to x3, with gain 1·s^{-1}·1·1=s^{-1}. The individual loops include: L1 is formed by s^{-1} from x2 to x3 and the -4 feedback, L1=-4s^{-1}; L2 is formed by the upper 1 from x2 to x3 and the -4 feedback, L2=-4; L3 is formed by x1 to x2 to x3 passing through two s^{-1} and the -2 feedback, L3=-2s^{-2}; L4 is formed by x1 to x2 and then through the upper 1 to x3 and the -2 feedback, L4=-2s^{-1}. All loops touch one another, and all touch the forward paths, so there is no product of non-touching loops, and Delta_k=1 for each forward path. Mason's formula gives Delta=1-(L1+L2+L3+L4)=1-(-4s^{-1}-4-2s^{-2}-2s^{-1})=5+6s^{-1}+2s^{-2}. Therefore Y(s)/U(s)=(P1+P2)/Delta=(s^{-2}+s^{-1})/(5+6s^{-1}+2s^{-2})=(s+1)/(5s^2+6s+2).
